Bacteria isolated from crude oil-dwelling bacteria tend to produce biosurfactants, the well-known antifungal compounds. Assembly BioSample Description Title: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens isolated from seeds of wheat cultivar Kanchan
Assembly BioSample Description Comment: Wheat blast, caused by a fungus Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum pathotype, has been a threat to wheat production in Brazil and some countries in South America since its first emergence in Parana state of Brazil in 1985. In February 2016, it emerged for the first time in Bangladesh and devastated more than 15,000 hectares of wheat in a large area of the South-western and western parts of Bangladesh. At present, it is unclear whether resistant wheat varieties against M. oryzae are available and the degree to which fungicide application for the neck blast management is reliable. Applications of plant probiotic bacteria are known to promote growth of host plants and suppress phytopathogenic fungi by various mechanisms. However, there are no biocontrol agents so far developed against the wheat blast fungus. To find potential biocontrol agents, we screened several hundreds of plant probiotic bacteria isolated from the surface sterilized seeds and organs of various crop plants including wheat and rice in Bangladesh. Some of the isolates including Bacillus amyloliquefaciens strain BTLK6A displayed potent inhibitory activities against the wheat blast fungus in vitro and suppression of disease in vivo. We sequenced this bacterial isolate and assembled the genome using the services provided by MicrobesNG.

Assembly BioSample Description Comment: Root-knot nematodes (RKNs; Meloidogyne spp.), as one of the most economically important plant-parasitic nematodes (PPNs), cause severe yield and quality losses in agriculture annually. Application of beneficial rhizobacterium like Bacillus genus is an environmental-safely and effective alternative to control RKNs. Here, we isolated a Bacillus velezensis strain YS-AT-DS1 (Bv-DS1) from the tidal soil. In vitro laboratory assays indicated that Bv-DS1 displayed the obvious antifugal activities against Rhizoctonia solani, Fusarium avenaceum and Fusarium graminearum, as well as the nematicidal activity against Meloidogyne incognita. Thus, Bv-DS1 strain could be used to exploit a biocontrol agent for RKN control in sustainable agriculture.
